title: Electronic Orbital Angular Momentum Driven by Finite-Momentum Phonons: Beyond Chiral and Axial Phonons
authors: Yongho Park, Jeonghun Sohn, Sejoong Kim, Kyoung-Whan Kim
abstract: We show that finite-momentum phonons generate electronic orbital angular momentum (OAM) even without phonon axiality or chirality, with the response controlled by the phonon wave vector $q$ and frequency $ω$. We develop a general gauge-field theory in which a unitary transformation absorbs the phonon displacement into emergent vector and scalar potentials acting on the electrons, providing a perturbative classification of the OAM response in $q$ and $ω$. We derive $q$- and $ω$-scaling laws for AC and DC responses. Notably, AC OAM arises even for linearly polarized phonons, with its magnitude and sign tunable by $q$. Its generation is governed by the matching between the phonon geometry and the electronic orbital texture rather than solely by the phonon angular momentum. The connection of the DC response to the electronic Berry curvature further supports that phonon angular momentum is not the only degree of freedom governing electronic OAM generation. Time-dependent tight-binding simulations under acoustic-phonon driving independently confirm the core predictions. Our results extend phonon-driven OAM beyond chiral and axial phonons and establish a wave-vector-tunable route to orbitronics, accessible with surface acoustic waves.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that electronic Orbital Angular Momentum can be generated by phonons even if those phonons lack inherent chirality or axial symmetry. By developing a gauge-field theory, the authors show that the OAM response is controlled by the phonon's wave vector and frequency, opening up a broad, tunable mechanism for orbitronics applications.
main_problem: The paper investigates the generation of electronic Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) induced by finite-momentum phonons, aiming to extend the understanding beyond mechanisms requiring chiral or axial phonon modes.
main_result: OAM can be generated by finite-momentum phonons even without phonon axiality or chirality, with the response being tunable by both the phonon wave vector (q) and frequency (ω). The generation mechanism is governed by the matching between phonon geometry and electronic orbital texture, not solely by phonon angular momentum.
method: The authors develop a general gauge-field theory using a unitary transformation to absorb phonon displacements into emergent vector and scalar potentials, allowing for a perturbative classification of the OAM response.
model_or_system: The study models electrons in a deformable lattice subjected to phonon displacement fields, analyzed using a local Bloch description and extended to quasi-two-dimensional tight-binding simulations.
key_observables: Electronic Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), AC and DC orbital polarization, and the connection to the electronic Berry curvature.
important_parameters: Phonon wave vector (q), phonon frequency (ω), and the phonon polarization (e.g., linear vs. circular).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the small displacement approximation and the long-wavelength limit for the phonon field.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling laws for AC OAM (linear in qω) and the DC component (quadratic in qω) for various phonon polarizations, confirming the theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using gauge potentials, derives scaling laws for AC and DC responses, and confirms the predictions using both analytical derivations and time-dependent tight-binding simulations.
why_interesting: This work provides a general, wave-vector-tunable route to generating orbital currents and OAM in condensed matter systems using acoustic phonons, which is highly relevant for designing novel orbitronics devices.
